answer_text:
# 🦴 Bones of the Head (Human Skull)

The human skull is generally considered to consist of **22 bones** — **8 cranial bones** and **14 facial skeleton bones**. This number rises to **29 bones** if the hyoid bone and three auditory ossicles (incus, malleus, and stapes) are included.

The skull is divided into two regions: the **neurocranium** (which protects the brain) and the **viscerocranium** (which forms the face).

---

## 🧠 Part 1: The Neurocranium (Cranial Bones) — 8 Bones

The cranium is composed of the **eight cranial bones**: the **frontal bone**, a **parietal bone** on each side, a **temporal bone** on each side, the **occipital bone**, the **ethmoid bone**, and the **sphenoid bone**.

Here is a breakdown of each:

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Frontal Bone** (×1) | A single, seamless bone that gives the forehead its structure. |
| **Parietal Bones** (×2) | The parietal bones form the sides and uppermost portion of the dome of the cranium. |
| **Temporal Bones** (×2) | The temporal bone forms the lower lateral side of the skull. The temporal bones subdivide into petrous, squamous, zygomatic, and mastoid parts; the petrous portion houses the inner ear. |
| **Occipital Bone** (×1) | The base of the cranium is the occipital bone, which has a central opening (foramen magnum) to admit the spinal cord. |
| **Sphenoid Bone** (×1) | A single bone below and in front of the brain, but behind the bones making up the face. It also forms part of the lower rear of the eye sockets. |
| **Ethmoid Bone** (×1) | Along with the sphenoid, it makes up the cranial floor. |

---

## 😊 Part 2: The Facial Skeleton (Viscerocranium) — 14 Bones

The facial skeleton supports the soft tissues of the face and consists of **14 bones**, which fuse to house the orbits of the eyes, the nasal and oral cavities, and the sinuses.

The bones of the facial skeleton (14) are the **vomer**, two **inferior nasal conchae**, two **nasal bones**, two **maxilla**, the **mandible**, two **palatine bones**, two **zygomatic bones**, and two **lacrimal bones**.

| Bone | Description |
|------|-------------|
| **Mandible** (×1) | The mandible (lower jaw) is the only moveable bone of the skull. |
| **Maxilla** (×2) | The two maxilla bones, one on the left and one on the right, form the top jaw and anchor the upper teeth. |
| **Zygomatic Bones** (×2) | The zygomatic (or malar) bones are the cheekbones, which join with the temporal and maxillary bones to form the zygomatic arch below the eye socket. |
| **Nasal Bones** (×2) | Form the bridge of the nose. |
| **Palatine Bones** (×2) | The two palatine bones form the roof of the mouth and help to form the mouth cavity. |
| **Lacrimal Bones** (×2) | Small bones forming part of the medial wall of the orbit (eye socket). |
| **Inferior Nasal Conchae** (×2) | The nasal cavity is formed by the vomer and the nasal, lacrimal, and turbinate (conchae) bones. |
| **Vomer** (×1) | Forms the lower part of the nasal septum. |

---

## 🔗 How the Bones Are Joined — Sutures

Sutures are a type of fibrous joint that are unique to the skull. They are immovable and fuse completely around the age of 20. The main sutures are:

- **Coronal suture** – fuses the frontal bone with the two parietal bones.
- **Sagittal suture** – fuses both parietal bones to each other.
- **Lambdoid suture** – fuses the occipital bone to the two parietal bones.

---

## 👶 In Infants

In neonates, the incompletely fused suture joints give rise to membranous gaps between the bones known as **fontanelles**. The two major ones are: the **frontal fontanelle** (at the junction of the coronal and sagittal sutures) and the **occipital fontanelle** (at the junction of the sagittal and lambdoid sutures).

---

> **Summary:** The skull has **22 bones** (8 cranial + 14 facial), all fused by sutures except the **mandible**, which is the only movable bone of the head.
